findings.highlight: I’m going to take a walk.
findings.governingReading: Shirou says only that he is going out briefly.
findings.explanation: The English invents a recreational walk and conceals that he is leaving to check on Sakura.

findings.highlight: Ohwell, I was just close by
findings.governingReading: “Ah—no, no particular reason.” Shirou evasively corrects himself before offering the nearby excuse.
findings.explanation: The English fuses “Oh” and “well” and drops the self-correction and professed lack of a reason.

findings.evidenceJa: その顔は本心からのもので
findings.governingReading: Her expression is heartfelt and genuine.
findings.explanation: Physical size replaces the narration’s judgment that Sakura’s smile comes from her true feelings.

findings.highlight: it doesn’t look like Shinji’s forcing her.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二に無理やり連れ戻されたようには見えなかった。
findings.governingReading: She does not look as though Shinji forcibly made her return home.
findings.explanation: The completed coercive return becomes vague ongoing force in the present.

findings.highlight: it is true that Shinji hasn’t done anything to Sakura.
findings.evidenceJa: 慎二のヤツが桜に何も話していないのは本当だった。
findings.governingReading: It is true that Shinji has told Sakura nothing about the situation.
findings.explanation: A claim about withholding information becomes the much broader claim that Shinji has done nothing to Sakura.

findings.governingReading: Shirou blurts out that he is relieved.
findings.explanation: The active simultaneous line replaces his emotional relief with generic approval.

findings.governingReading: Their vacant mutual stare lasts more than ten seconds—ten-odd seconds.
findings.explanation: “About ten” permits less than ten and loses the source’s ten-plus duration.

findings.governingReading: Shirou begins, “...Then, Sakura—” before their simultaneous requests.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the unfinished address that sets up the comic overlap.

findings.highlight: I won’t be able to go to your house
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩のお家に行くのは遠慮します。
findings.governingReading: Sakura politely says she will refrain from going to Shirou’s house.
findings.explanation: Her deferential choice becomes an external inability.

findings.evidenceJa: 怒りながらも俺を待っていたセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber, though angry, has waited for Shirou at the entrance.
findings.explanation: mirror moon replaces Saber’s name and identity with the masculine generic “swordsman,” while losing the concessive force of her waiting despite anger.

findings.highlight: at the entranceand I told her
findings.evidenceJa: 玄関で怒りながらも俺を待っていた
findings.governingReading: She was waiting at the entrance despite her anger.
findings.explanation: The English visibly joins “entrance” and “and,” corrupting the sentence boundary.

findings.highlight: I don’t want her to consider him as an enemy
findings.evidenceJa: 敵と認識する事は避けたかったからだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou himself wanted to avoid recognizing or designating Shinji as an enemy until Shinji’s intentions became clear.
findings.explanation: The English transfers the judgment to Saber, weakening Shirou’s deliberate reluctance to classify his friend as an enemy.

findings.governingReading: Shirou has not had Fuji-nee’s cooking since he himself was a kid.
findings.explanation: The plural “we” also places Fuji-nee in childhood and changes their age relationship.
